subject: maths
title: Forming expressions from words and patterns

lines.say: Writing algebra from words is like translating into another language.
Sum, more than, increased by: all mean add. 5 more than n is n plus 5.
Product, times, twice: all mean multiply. Twice n is 2n.
Less than flips the order. 7 less than 3n is 3n minus 7.
Shared equally by 4 means divide. n over 4.
The sum of n and 5, multiplied by 4. Add first, then multiply.
4n plus 5 means something different. If words group two things, bracket them.
Three times the sum of a number and 4, minus twice the number.
Expand and collect. 3n plus 12 minus 2n is n plus 12.
Check with n equals 1. 15 minus 2 is 13. And 1 plus 12 is 13.
Consecutive numbers go up by 1: n, n plus 1, n plus 2.
An even number is 2n. An odd number is 2n plus 1.
Add three consecutive numbers. You get 3n plus 3.
That's 3 lots of n plus 1. So it's always a multiple of 3.
Check: 6 plus 7 plus 8 is 21, which is 3 times 7.
One square of matchsticks uses 4 sticks.

draw.alt: One square made of four matchsticks

lines.say: Add a second square. It only needs 3 more sticks.

draw.alt: Two squares: three new sticks added

lines.say: And 3 more again. 4, 7, 10. The common difference is 3.

draw.alt: Three squares: three more sticks added

lines.say: Multiply n by the difference, 3. Step back one term from 4 to get 1.
Shape 50 needs 3 times 50 plus 1. That's 151 sticks.
Which shape uses 100? Take 1, then divide by 3. Shape 33.
A taxi charges 4.20 to start, plus 2.10 per kilometre.
For k kilometres, the cost is 4.2 plus 2.1k dollars.
For 12 kilometres: 4.2 plus 25.2 is 29.40 dollars.
5, 9, 13 is not 4n plus 5. It's 4n plus 1.
One case working isn't enough. Check two.
Less than flips.
Sum of, then times, means brackets.
Difference times n, then fix the start.
Count two shapes to check any rule.
